sentences.text:
LABOUR  MALAKCHHAR THANA SHAHPURA DISTRICT  JABALPUR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAKESH TIWARI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION SHAHPURA DISTRICT JABALPUR (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI ANIL UPADHYAY - PANEL LAWYER)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the  following:
 ORDER This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C filed on behalf of applicant for grant of bail,
pending trial.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.424/2022 o f Police Station Shahpura,
District Jabalpur for commission of offence punishable under Section 376(D) of IPC.
He is in detention since 20.10.2022.
As per prosecution story on 19.10.2022, at around 12:59 AM, 22 years old prosecutrix lodged an FIR alleging that she was married to Gorelal 2 years ago.
Gorelal after consuming liquor used to beat her.
She had called her parents for making complaint against her husband.
After leaving of her parents for their home, Gorelal again beat her.

She had gone to Shahpura police station for lodging FIR, in the meantime, her husband along with her brother-in-law also came there, at around 12:00 Mangal Barman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26485932/
1 of midnight 100 number vehicle had dropped them ahead Chaprat.

sentences.text: On the way to Bansipur two relatives of her brother in law, residents of Malkachar came there from motorcycle, her husband caught hold her and her brother-in-law and two others repeatedly committed rape upon her.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C has made specific allegation against her husband, Ramnath, Suraj and Dinesh.
In her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. she has not named Mangal.
He has been enroped in offence without any proof.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail, pending the trial.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that in supplementary statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C it has been made clear that the person who was involved in commission of rape was not Suraj but Mangal.
Therefore, he be not released on bail.
Applicant and other accused persons are husband and relatives of prosecutrix.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C she has not named present applicant.

Therefore, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, but having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Mangal Barman be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Mangal Barman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26485932/
